key_insight: SMAW produced an acceptable low-carbon steel pipeline weld with adequate penetration and no cracking in bend tests, indicating generally good weld integrity.
engineering_relevance: The results support SMAW as a viable repair or fabrication method for low-carbon steel pipelines when mechanical performance and joint quality are verified.
method: Destructive testing of the welded joint: hardness, tensile, impact-Charpy, and bend tests.
Macro/micro hardness and macro inspection to assess weld metal, HAZ, and base metal behavior.
Measured weld geometry and penetration depth to confirm fusion quality.
evidence_signal: The weld showed UTS values of 569.26 and 566.52 N/mm², Charpy impact averages of 132.9 J (WM), 237.1 J (HAZ), and 247.4 J (BM), and adequate penetration of about 5.8 mm.
watch_item: Results come from a limited set of samples, so field application should still account for variability in welding conditions and service loading.
paper_title: Investigation of Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)Weld Integrity on a Low- Carbon Steel Pipeline using Destructive Mechanical Testing Technique
